assessment: This paper addresses the important question of how the cerebellum transforms multiple streams of sensory information into an estimate of the motion of the body in the world. The authors find that Purkinje cells, the inhibitory principal neurons of the cerebellar cortex, have multimodal and highly diverse responses to vestibular and neck proprioceptive inputs. Notably, this information is combined in a way that is different from what is seen in downstream fastigial neurons, which reflect either head or body motion, but not both.
